recentItems.title: How the Houthi advance in Yemen could disrupt global trade | DW News
recentItems.description:
Yemen's Houthi rebel forces have seized control of the strategic port city of Mocha, on Yemen's Red Sea coast. The move puts the Iran-backed rebel group closer to controlling the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key chokepoint for global trade. Shipping routes have already come under pressure as a result of the ongoing war between the US and Iran and its effect on another vital bottleneck: the Strait of Hormuz. Now oil prices have jumped to over $100 a barrel again — the highest price in the last two months.
If you want to know more about the Houthis' advance and its repercussions, check out our coverage here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xkM6HY5gdkY

recentItems.title: Did jet fuel melt the steel beams on 9/11? | DW News
recentItems.description:
9/11 Truthers are right about one thing: Fire from jet fuel cannot melt steel beams. But: Steel doesn't need to melt to lose stability.
 
As with any conspiracy theory, there are many arguments that need to be debunked. 

They found molten metal in the rubble, so something other than fire must have melted it. 
True - but no analysis ever confirmed it was structural steel. Skyscrapers are full of other metals: aluminum from the aircraft, elevator systems, wiring. Aluminum melts around 660°C, way below the fire temps recorded at Ground Zero. NIST's conclusion: It’s most likely melted aluminum, not steel. 

You can see explosions during the collapse. 
Those bursts of dust and smoke shooting out of windows are real - but they're not explosives. Once the upper floors began falling, that mass slammed into the floors below, faster than the trapped air could escape. Air, smoke, and debris got forced out sideways through windows, floor by floor, just ahead of the collapse - like a piston. 

WTC 7 wasn't even hit by a plane - and it still collapsed. 
WTC 7 stood about 370 feet from the Twin Towers. When the North Tower (WTC 1) collapsed, building parts crashed into WTC 7's structure and knocked out the water supply firefighters needed to fight the fires. Those fires burned uncontrolled for almost 7 hours. The official investigation found that heat from the fires caused a critical support beam to expand and slip off its column. That triggered a cascading floor failure that left the column unsupported; when it buckled, the whole building came down. It's the first known case of fire alone bringing down a high-rise.  

FAQ of the official investigation: 
https://www.nist.gov/world-trade-center-investigation/study-faqs/wtc-towers-investigation

recentItems.title: Why South Africa's 'Dr. Death' is making headlines again | DW News
recentItems.description:
A sold-out appearance by Wouter Basson, the former head of South Africa's apartheid-era chemical and biological warfare program, has reignited a fierce debate about accountability, memory and free speech. 

Known by critics as "Dr Death," Basson led the secretive "Project Coast" program during the final years of apartheid. He later faced accusations linked to the development of lethal toxins and other covert operations. Although Basson denied wrongdoing and was acquitted of criminal charges in 2002, his legacy remains deeply controversial. 

In this video, we examine Basson's role in "Project Coast," the legal cases that followed apartheid, and the public backlash over his latest appearance. Should controversial figures be given a platform, or does doing so risk normalizing a troubling past? 

#dwafrica #dwcurrentaffairs #southafrica
